# Base Image: Use Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a modern, stable C++ and MPI environment.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variable to ensure package managers run without interactive prompts.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install all necessary dependencies in a single layer to optimize image size.
# This includes the C/++ toolchain, certificates for HTTPS git access, cmake, and OpenMPI.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure OpenMPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes on AWS.
# This ensures MPI uses the TCP network interface for inter-node communication
# and disables fabric-specific transports (like InfiniBand/openib) that are not present.
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=tcp,self
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set a working directory for cloning and building the application.
WORKDIR /opt/build

# Clone Kripke from the 'master' branch, which is the repository's main branch.
# The '--recursive' flag ensures all submodules (like BLT) are cloned.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recursive --branch master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git

# Set the working directory to the cloned source code.
WORKDIR /opt/build/Kripke

# Configure, build, and install the Kripke application.
# - A separate 'build' directory is created to keep the source tree clean.
# - CMake is configured for a Release build for performance.
# - MPI and OpenMP are enabled for parallel execution on multi-core CPU nodes.
# - CUDA is explicitly disabled as this is a CPU-only build.
# - CORRECTION: The build produces 'kripke.exe'. The cp command is updated to copy the correct file.
#   The executable is copied to /usr/local/bin/kripke to make it available on the system's PATH.
RUN mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake .. \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
    -DENABLE_OPENMP=ON \
    -DENABLE_CUDA=OFF && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke

# Clean up the build directory to reduce final image size.
RUN rm -rf /opt/build

# Reset the working directory to provide a clean environment for container execution.
WORKDIR /

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke HPC benchmark
# on a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  # Deploy to the default namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run for the job.
  # Flux will schedule these tasks across the pods defined by 'size'.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error and print it to the logs.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # The application container definition.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The application command to run. The Flux Operator will automatically
      # prepend 'flux run -n <tasks>' to this command.
      # This runs a small Kripke problem suitable for a single node.
      command: kripke --nest 8,8,8 --groups 16 --zones 8,8,8

      # This main container is part of the job, not a separate pod to launch it.
      # The Flux broker and workers will run within this pod.
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest is optimized to run a larger Kripke benchmark
# on a specific high-performance AWS ARM64 instance (m7g.16xlarge).
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  # Deploy to the default namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run, matching the vCPU count of the target instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Fail on any error and print it to the logs.
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod-specific settings for scheduling and execution environment.
  pod:
    # Schedule this MiniCluster only on nodes with the specified instance type.
    # This targets a 64-core ARM-based Graviton processor instance.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and execution environment.
  flux:
    container:
      # Specify an ARM-compatible image for the Flux broker/view, as the
      # nodeSelector targets an ARM64 architecture (AWS Graviton).
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # The application container definition.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Corrected and scaled-up command for Kripke.
      # --procs defines the MPI task layout (4x4x4=64 tasks).
      # --groups, --zones, and --gset are increased to create a larger problem
      # suitable for a 64-core machine to maximize grind time.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --groups 128 --zones 64,64,64 --gset 8

      # This main container is part of the job, not a separate pod to launch it.
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest runs a Kripke benchmark, corrected after a previous
# Out of Memory (OOM) failure. The problem size has been reduced to fit within
# the memory limits of the target HPC instance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run, matching the vCPU count of the target instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod-specific settings for scheduling and execution environment.
  pod:
    # Schedule this MiniCluster only on nodes with the specified instance type.
    # This targets a 64-core ARM-based Graviton processor instance specialized for HPC.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific settings for the broker and execution environment.
  flux:
    container:
      # Specify an ARM-compatible image for the Flux broker/view, as the
      # nodeSelector targets an ARM64 architecture (AWS Graviton).
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # The application container definition.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # Command adjusted to prevent OOM errors. The --zones parameter was reduced
      # from 80 to 64 to decrease the application's memory footprint, allowing it
      # to run successfully on the hpc7g.16xlarge node.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --groups 256 --zones 64,64,64 --gset 16

      # This main container is part of the job, not a separate pod to launch it.
      launcher: false

# This MiniCluster manifest has been corrected to resolve a pod scheduling failure.
# The nodeSelector has been updated to an available AMD instance type (c7a.12xlarge),
# and all dependent parameters (tasks, command) have been adjusted accordingly.
# The ARM-specific Flux container image has been removed as it's no longer needed.

kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # Updated tasks to match the 48 vCPUs of the new c7a.12xlarge instance.
  tasks: 48

  # Defines logging behavior for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Do not delete the pods after the job completes to allow for log inspection.
  cleanup: false

  # Pod-specific settings for scheduling and execution environment.
  pod:
    # Switched to an available AMD instance type to fix the scheduling failure.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # The application container definition.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The processor geometry (--procs) is updated to 4x4x3 to match the new task count of 48.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --groups 256 --zones 64,64,64 --gset 16

      # This main container is part of the job, not a separate pod to launch it.
      launcher: false

  # The number of pods in the MiniCluster, set to 1 to run on a single node.
